s0003.literal: Zhao Zhili; Cai Jingli; Liu Shizhi; Xie Qi
s0003.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili; Cai Jingli; Liu Shizhi; Xie Qi

s0005.literal: Zhao Zhili, styled Qidan, was a native of Longxi in Tianshui.
s0005.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili, styled Qidan, came from Longxi in Tianshui.

s0006.literal: His father Xiaomu was magistrate of Houguan under Liang.
s0006.idiomatic: His father Xiaomu had been magistrate of Houguan under Liang.

s0007.literal: Zhili ranged through literature and history and was skilled at clerical script.
s0007.idiomatic: Zhili read widely in literature and history and wrote a fine clerical hand.

s0008.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended him and he was brought in as record-office aide.
s0008.idiomatic: When the Founder marched against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended him and he was made record-office aide.

s0009.literal: Zhili's writing was ample and swift; whenever he took dictation for military documents, his brush finished at once and nearly all pleased the ruler.
s0009.idiomatic: Zhili wrote copiously and fast. Dictated army papers left his brush finished in one pass, and almost all pleased the Founder.

s0010.literal: From this he constantly attended at the ruler's side and was deeply entrusted; of the plans of the time none in which he did not take part therein.
s0010.idiomatic: From then on he was always at the Founder's side, deeply trusted, and party to every plan of the day.

s0011.literal: Editorial footnote marker 1. Zhili also offered much counsel for correction and replacement.
s0011.idiomatic: [1] He also offered much counsel on policy.

s0012.literal: When the Founder pacified Hou Jing and the army reached Baimao Bay, the memorials to Emperor Yuan of Liang and the missives with Wang Senbian discussing military affairs were all composed by Zhili.
s0012.idiomatic: When the Founder crushed Hou Jing and the army reached Baimao Bay, the memorials to Emperor Yuan of Liang and the letters to Wang Senbian on military affairs were all Zhili's work.

s0013.literal: Zhili was calm and possessed of stratagem; whenever there were great affairs of state and army, Emperor Wen would send sealed letters to ask him.
s0013.idiomatic: Zhili was quiet and shrewd. On every grave matter of state or army, Emperor Wen sent sealed letters to ask his view.

s0014.literal: When his term expired he was made General of Manifest Prestige and Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
s0014.idiomatic: When his term ended he was made General of Manifest Prestige and right commandant of the heir apparent's guard.

s0015.literal: He was transferred to Right Guard General and concurrently Front Army General.
s0015.idiomatic: He was transferred to right guard general and also front army general.

s0016.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged forty-seven.
s0016.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died, at forty-seven.

s0017.literal: An edict posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant, posthumous title Loyal.
s0017.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant with the posthumous name Loyal.

s0021.literal: Cai Jingli, styled Maoshi, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
s0021.idiomatic: Cai Jingli, styled Maoshi, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

s0022.literal: His grandfather Dian was Master of the Left for the People under Liang.
s0022.idiomatic: His grandfather Dian had been master of the left for the people under Liang.

s0023.literal: His father Datong was record-office aide to the Prince of Yueyang, Light Chariots, and managed metropolitan selection.
s0023.idiomatic: His father Datong was record-office aide to the Prince of Yueyang of the Light Chariots establishment and ran metropolitan appointments.

s0024.literal: Jingli in youth was handsome and alert and showed filial conduct.
s0024.idiomatic: Jingli in youth was bright and open, and known for filial piety.

s0025.literal: His family was poor yet he loved learning; he was skilled at letters and excelled at cursive and clerical script.
s0025.idiomatic: Though poor he loved learning, wrote excellent letters, and excelled at cursive and clerical script.

s0026.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as aide in princely establishments, went out as magistrate of Haiyang, and his governance won a name for ability.
s0026.idiomatic: He entered service as a princely aide, then became magistrate of Haiyang, where his rule won a name for competence.

s0027.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Jianwen of Liang was imprisoned by Jing; Jingli with the heir of Nankang, Xiao Huili, plotted to seize the emperor and flee, but the affair leaked and he was seized; the rebel partisan Wang Wei protected him and he escaped death.
s0027.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Jianwen was held by Jing. Jingli and the heir of Nankang, Xiao Huili, plotted to carry the emperor off, but the plot was discovered and he was arrested. The rebel Wang Wei shielded him and he survived.

s0028.literal: He then traveled as a guest to Jingkou.
s0028.idiomatic: He then wandered as a guest to Jingkou.

s0029.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified the Founder garrisoned Zhufang and, having long heard his name, summoned him by letter.
s0029.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell the Founder held Zhufang, had long heard of him, and summoned him by letter.

s0030.literal: Jingli replied to the envoy's letter; his brush never paused and the text needed no revision.
s0030.idiomatic: Jingli answered the envoy's letter without lifting his brush and without a single revision.

s0032.literal: I have received your gracious letter, bending low to summon me; reading it over and again, I am deeply glad.
s0032.idiomatic: I have received your gracious letter, summoning me with such kindness. Reading it again and again, I am deeply glad.

s0033.literal: I venture to think that the age seeks famous steeds; on good ground they run a thousand li; the time delights in rare treasures; on the carriage mirror there is already an inch-sized gem.
s0033.idiomatic: The age seeks famous steeds that can run a thousand li on good ground; the time delights in rare jewels, and already on the carriage mirror there is a gem an inch across.

s0034.literal: But now Yun Xian plays, and of themselves the Bayu dances cease; catalpa and paulownia are being carved—how could one look to the stables for fodder?
s0034.idiomatic: Yet now Yun Xian plays, and of themselves the Bayu dances cease; catalpa and paulownia are being carved—who would still look to the stables for fodder?

s0035.literal: Looking up to the Illustrious General, Lord, and Marquis under your command: your talent stands tall, your heroic bearing splendid; the age meets hard fortune and your will sets right many calamities; you shake Mount Heng and pacify the Five Ridges, cleanse the Chan source and clarify the nine streams; armored troops number a hundred thousand, strong crossbows several thousand; you swear the army that will restore the throne and gather the power of righteous men; whale and crocodile are cut down, the campaign does not exceed its season, mist and fog are cleared, and soldiers need no bloody blades.
s0035.idiomatic: Looking up to you, Illustrious General, Lord, and Marquis: talent in full flower, bearing heroic and bright; fortune is hard and your will sets the realm right; you shake Mount Heng and pacify the Five Ridges, cleanse the Chan headwaters and clear the nine streams; a hundred thousand armored men, thousands of strong crossbows; you swear the army that will restore the throne and gather righteous men; enemies are cut down in a campaign that does not outlast its season, the air clears, and soldiers win without bloody blades.

s0036.literal: Though Han executed Lu and Chan and the whole court truly relied on the Marquis of Jiang, and Jin attacked Yue and Jun and within and without alike depended on Tao Kan, comparing affairs and weighing merit, how could those be reckoned?
s0036.idiomatic: When Han executed Lu and Chan the whole court truly leaned on the Marquis of Jiang; when Jin struck Su and Jun the court within and without alike leaned on Tao Kan—set beside your deeds, what are those worth reckoning?

s0037.literal: Moreover you display might in Yan and the eastern lands; caps and coaches pass the northern gate; you array banners in Xu and song overflows the eastern road; you can make border posts lay aside their drums, travelers sleep in the open, lanes lose nothing left behind, markets show no strange prices—vast indeed are your merit, virtue, government, and transformation, unmatched since antiquity, surely not something shallow men could exhaust in telling.
s0037.idiomatic: You show might in Yan and the eastern lands; nobles pass the northern gate; you array banners in Xu and song fills the eastern road; border posts lay aside their drums, travelers sleep in the open, no one picks up what another drops, markets hold no strange prices—your merit, virtue, and rule are vast beyond antiquity, not something a shallow man could tell to the end.

s0038.literal: Therefore the people of the realm turn to your wind and admire your righteousness; heel to toe they open their robes and come in throngs.
s0038.idiomatic: So the people of the realm turn to your wind and admire your righteousness; heel to toe they open their robes and crowd in.

s0039.literal: Some are noble scions of the imperial house, honored wanderers of fine reputation, splendid talents of Qi and Chu, precocious youths of Jing and Wu.
s0039.idiomatic: Some are noble scions of the house, honored wanderers of fine name, splendid talents of Qi and Chu, precocious youths of Jing and Wu.

s0040.literal: As warriors they bristle with fierce spirit, ambition seizing the four quarters; on land they uproot mountains, on water they cut dragons; with six-jun bows they shoot left and right; with ten-thousand-man swords they close in hand to hand; storming ramparts like Wen Yang, burning ships like Huang Gai; a hundred battles, a hundred victories; troops like pi-xiu gather in hosts.
s0040.idiomatic: Warriors bristle with fierce spirit and ambition fills the four quarters; on land they uproot mountains, on water they cut dragons; six-jun bows shoot left and right; ten-thousand-man swords close hand to hand; they storm ramparts like Wen Yang and burn ships like Huang Gai; a hundred battles, a hundred victories; hosts gather like pi-xiu.

s0041.literal: As men of letters they are broadly learned Confucians, men of outstanding talent and great vessel; their ornamented prose shines and their brushwork weaves brocade; Yang Xiong cannot match their pens, Yu Xin cannot surpass their records; a letter flies and Liaocheng falls; pure talk rises and Ying's army retreats.
s0041.idiomatic: Scholars are broadly learned, men of great talent and vessel; their ornamented prose shines and their brushwork weaves brocade; Yang Xiong cannot match their pens, Yu Xin cannot surpass their records; a letter flies and Liaocheng falls; pure talk rises and Ying's army retreats.

s0042.literal: Again there are debaters of Sanhe who change grief and joy in an instant, and strategists of the Six Wonders who reverse sudden change in a flash.
s0042.idiomatic: There are debaters of Sanhe who change grief and joy in an instant, and strategists of the Six Wonders who reverse sudden change in a flash.

s0043.literal: They govern the people like Zijian and set foot in a district with success; they judge cases like Zhong You and a single phrase decides right.
s0043.idiomatic: They govern like Zijian and wherever they step succeed; they judge like Zhong You and a single phrase decides right.

s0044.literal: In straight speech they are like Mao Sui and can stiffen their lord's majesty; as envoys they are like Xiang Ru and do not disgrace their ruler's charge.
s0044.idiomatic: In straight speech they are like Mao Sui and stiffen their lord's majesty; as envoys they are like Xiang Ru and do not disgrace their ruler's charge.

s0045.literal: Cherishing loyalty and embracing righteousness, grateful they give themselves; sincerity cuts through gold, spirit pierces the white sun; heroes within the seas—all are gathered in your net.
s0045.idiomatic: Loyal and righteous, grateful they give themselves; sincerity cuts gold, spirit pierces the white sun; heroes within the seas—all are gathered in your net.

s0046.literal: The Illustrious General leaves saddle and dismounts, pushes aside his desk and stops eating, extends rank to honor them and builds lodges to settle them—light with wealth, heavy with spirit, humble in body and thick toward scholars—how grand! how grand!
s0046.idiomatic: You leave saddle and dismount, push aside your desk and stop eating, extend rank to honor them and build lodges to settle them—light with wealth, heavy with spirit, humble in body and generous to scholars—how grand! how grand!

s0048.literal: I have also heard that in the Warring States generals and ministers all promoted guest companions; in middle antiquity governors and shepherds all lavishly extended staff—many officers, many scholars: thus the general's nobility is made.
s0048.idiomatic: I have also heard that in the Warring States generals and ministers all promoted guests; in middle antiquity governors lavishly extended staff—many officers, many scholars: thus a general's nobility is made.

s0049.literal: Only measure capacity and test truth, call talent and assign office, round pegs in round holes and square in square, each fulfilling his fit; entrusted with charge and held to completion—who would not give full force?
s0049.idiomatic: Only measure capacity and test truth, call talent and assign office, round pegs in round holes and square in square, each in his fit; entrusted with charge and held to completion—who would not give full force?

s0050.literal: As for a runner of low rank, I am but a vain and mediocre man.
s0050.idiomatic: As for me, a runner of low rank, I am but a vain and mediocre man.

s0051.literal: Reading books autumn and winter, in the end I am ashamed before true scholarship; wielding the brush as clerk, in the end I lack a special grade.
s0051.idiomatic: I read books autumn and winter and in the end am ashamed before true scholarship; I wield the brush as clerk and in the end lack a special grade.

s0052.literal: A humble gate, declining and plain, with no path to fame; a petty office and light means—how could I reach far?
s0052.idiomatic: My gate is humble and plain, with no path to fame; my office petty and my means light—how could I reach far?

s0053.literal: Since the yang-nine met obstruction and Heaven's step was hard, like those honored officials I drowned in the great bandit, repeatedly neared peril, and fully trod thin ice.
s0053.idiomatic: Since the yang-nine met obstruction and Heaven's step was hard, like those honored officials I drowned in the great bandit, repeatedly neared peril, and fully trod thin ice.

s0054.literal: Now the royal way is reviving, anxious care opens fortune; to preserve this slight life is already great fortune; I am just now glad for drink and peck—this is what men call returning to life.
s0054.idiomatic: Now the royal way revives and anxious care opens fortune; to preserve this slight life is already great fortune; I am just now glad for drink and peck—this is what men call returning to life.

s0055.literal: Yet the imperial carriage has not returned; Wan and Luo lie waste; on four walls remain only the leavings of three armies; through long summer there is not half a bean's yield; wandering among old friends, I borrow for a time; having reached this happy land, truly beautiful—I forget to return.
s0055.idiomatic: Yet the imperial carriage has not returned; Wan and Luo lie waste; four walls hold only the leavings of three armies; through long summer not half a bean's yield; wandering among old friends I borrow for a time; having reached this happy land, truly beautiful—I forget to return.

s0056.literal: Privately I admire your high righteousness and for a time visit your gate; the Illustrious General has lowered your countenance; two or three scholar friends lend their surplus talk; you do not discard rush and reeds and send a letter bidding me stay—you would set chickens and ducks in the pool with mandarin ducks and swans, and move rubble to share the price of gold and jade.
s0056.idiomatic: Privately I admire your high righteousness and for a time visit your gate; you have lowered your countenance; two or three scholar friends lend their surplus talk; you do not discard rush and reeds and send a letter bidding me stay—you would set chickens and ducks in the pool with mandarin ducks and swans, and move rubble to share the price of gold and jade.

s0057.literal: Formerly Zengzi with broken ribs wandered in Qin and suddenly met Pan Cai; carrying matting he entered Zhao and at once was detained—today though I am a sojourner, compared with that it is not equal; the burden of Fan Lin—how could I bear it?
s0057.idiomatic: Formerly Zengzi with broken ribs wandered in Qin and suddenly met Pan Cai; carrying matting he entered Zhao and at once was detained—today though I am a sojourner, compared with that it is not equal; the burden of Fan Lin—how could I bear it?

s0058.literal: Yet tiny convolvulus leans on tall pine to lift itself; foolish gnats trust the triple team's tail to run far.
s0058.idiomatic: Yet tiny convolvulus leans on tall pine to lift itself; foolish gnats trust the triple team's tail to run far.

s0059.literal: I venture without limit and wish to serve as your footman, to be hair on belly and back, and if released to join the number of barking dogs—added honor and changed view would already be much fortune.
s0059.idiomatic: I venture without limit and wish to serve as your footman, to be hair on belly and back, and if released to join the number of barking dogs—added honor and changed view would already be much fortune.

s0060.literal: The sea does not dislike depth; the mountain does not yield height; I dare lay out my inmost heart—may the General read it.
s0060.idiomatic: The sea does not dislike depth; the mountain does not yield height; I dare lay out my inmost heart—may you read it, General.

s0061.literal: The Founder received the letter and greatly admired it.
s0061.idiomatic: The Founder received the letter and admired it greatly.

s0062.literal: He again sent a letter in reply and the same day appointed him by provisional commission Record-Office Aide in the Northern Expedition headquarters, still heading the record office.
s0062.idiomatic: He sent another letter in reply and the same day appointed him record-office aide in the northern expedition headquarters, still heading the record office.

s0063.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang [Chang] was then administrator of Wuxing; Chang was still young, Editorial footnote marker 3. Wuxing was the prince's native commandery; elders and old friends observed rank by seniority; the Founder feared Chang was young and might receive them with improper courtesy, and so sent Jingli to assist him.
s0063.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chang was administering Wuxing. [3] He was still young. Wuxing was his home commandery; elders and old friends observed rank by seniority. The Founder feared the prince was young and might receive them with improper courtesy, and sent Jingli to assist him.

s0064.literal: In the Chengsheng era he was appointed Regular Attendant for Direct Communication and again managed the establishment record office.
s0064.idiomatic: In the Chengsheng era he was made regular attendant for direct communication and again ran the establishment record office.

s0065.literal: When the Founder was about to campaign against Wang Senbian he plotted alone with Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli did not know of it.
s0065.idiomatic: When the Founder was about to strike Wang Senbian he plotted alone with Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli knew nothing of it.

s0066.literal: When dispositions were complete he summoned him to draft the proclamation; Jingli took brush and finished at once; the wording was moving and all pleased the ruler.
s0066.idiomatic: When dispositions were complete he summoned him to draft the proclamation. Jingli took brush and finished at once; the wording was moving and all pleased the Founder.

s0067.literal: When Senbian was executed the Founder assisted the government and appointed Jingli Attendant of the Masters of Writing, still managing the record office as before.
s0067.idiomatic: When Senbian was killed the Founder assisted the government and made Jingli attendant of the masters of writing, still managing the record office.

s0068.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently managed the chancellor's record office.
s0068.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 1 (555) he was made attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate and also ran the chancellor's record office.

s0069.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Secretariat Communicating Affairs Attendant, and managed edicts and proclamations.
s0069.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne he was made director of the secretariat, secretariat communicating affairs attendant, and manager of edicts.

s0070.literal: In the second year of Yongding, because his wife's younger brother Liu Yan fraudulently accepted horses presented by Zhou Bao'an, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong and demoted to Secretariat Gentleman, his post as attendant unchanged.
s0070.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2 (558) his wife's younger brother Liu Yan was found to have fraudulently accepted horses from Zhou Bao'an; Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong impeached him and he was demoted to secretariat gentleman, keeping his post as attendant.

s0071.literal: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Jingli was recalled as Adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Pacifier of the East, and concurrently Grand Master of the Great Boats.
s0071.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Jingli was recalled as adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Pacifier of the East, and concurrently grand master of the great boats.

s0072.literal: Editorial footnote marker 5. When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was made General Who Overcomes the Enemy and army aide to Wu Mingche.
s0072.idiomatic: [5] When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was made General Who Overcomes the Enemy and army aide to Wu Mingche.

s0073.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Mingche on his own authority in the army executed Interior Magistrate of Ancheng Yang Wentong, and again accepted horses and weapons from surrendered men with unclear title; Jingli again was charged for failing to correct this and was arrested and handed over for trial.
s0073.idiomatic: When Jiao fell, Mingche on his own authority executed Interior Magistrate of Ancheng Yang Wentong in camp and accepted horses and weapons from surrendered men with unclear title; Jingli was again charged for failing to correct this and was arrested for trial.

s0074.literal: After a long time he was pardoned and recalled as Adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Pacifier of the East.
s0074.idiomatic: After a long time he was pardoned and recalled as adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Pacifier of the East.

s0075.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, as commander Wu Mingche marched north in expedition, wherever he went he won; he fought the Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Luliang, inflicted a great defeat, and beheaded and captured tens of thousands; he was about to advance and take Pengcheng.
s0075.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 (573) Commander Wu Mingche marched north and won wherever he went; he fought the Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Luliang, shattered him, and beheaded and captured tens of thousands; he was about to advance on Pengcheng.

s0076.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan was keen on the lands south of the Yellow River and thought command alone could settle them; Jingli remonstrated, saying the army was weary and the generals proud and that one should not press the distant strategy too far.
s0076.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was keen on the lands south of the Yellow River and thought command alone could settle them; Jingli remonstrated that the army was weary and the generals proud and that the distant strategy should not be pressed too far.

s0077.literal: Emperor Xuan hated his damping the men's spirit, was greatly angered, yet because he was an old minister of the court did not deeply punish him and sent him out as General of Far Illumination and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang.
s0077.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan hated his damping the men's spirit and was furious, yet because he was an old court minister did not punish him deeply and sent him out as General of Far Illumination and interior magistrate of Yuzhang.

s0078.literal: Before he departed he was impeached by flying memorial; because in his days at the capital his corruption was notorious, the emperor ordered the relevant offices to investigate, Editorial footnote marker 7. and Jingli admitted only half.
s0078.idiomatic: Before he could leave he was impeached by flying memorial; his corruption in the capital was notorious and the emperor ordered investigation. [7] Jingli admitted only half.

s0079.literal: Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao memorialized, saying: "Your servant has heard that in a gentleman's conduct loyalty serves his superiors and integrity holds his person; if he violates this way, punishment knows no pardon.
s0079.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao then memorialized: "I have heard that in a gentleman's conduct loyalty serves his superiors and integrity holds his person; if he violates this way, punishment knows no pardon.

s0080.literal: Your servant respectfully accuses General of Far Illumination and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang, Marquis of Xinfeng, Jingli: by many strokes of fortune he was early favored at the founding king's side; when the imperial fortune was lifting he took part in the founding structure.
s0080.idiomatic: I respectfully accuse General of Far Illumination and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang, Marquis of Xinfeng, Jingli: by many strokes of fortune he was early favored at the founding king's side; when the imperial fortune was lifting he took part in the founding structure.

s0081.literal: In the Tianjia era his bribes were notorious; by imperial grace he was recorded for use and allowed to sound again; fief land and lofty rank were not long in returning.
s0081.idiomatic: In the Tianjia era his bribes were notorious; by imperial grace he was recorded for use and allowed to sound again; fief land and lofty rank were not long in returning.

s0082.literal: He could not change his ways and encourage himself to repay partial formation; he then monopolized greed and corruption, manifest near and far—once was already too much; how could there be a second?
s0082.idiomatic: He could not change his ways and encourage himself to repay partial formation; he then monopolized greed and corruption, manifest near and far—once was already too much; how could there be a second?

s0083.literal: He should be placed in the penal code to clarify autumn law.
s0083.idiomatic: He should be placed in the penal code to clarify autumn law.

s0084.literal: Your servants jointly propose that, on the matter before us, Jingli be removed from the office he holds and the Court of Imperial Entertainments be directed to strip his fief land.
s0084.idiomatic: We jointly propose that, on the matter before us, Jingli be removed from the office he holds and the Court of Imperial Entertainments be directed to strip his fief.

s0085.literal: Respectfully presenting the white bamboo to inform."
s0085.idiomatic: Respectfully presenting the white bamboo to inform."

s0087.literal: Thereupon he was moved to live in Kuaiji.
s0087.idiomatic: Thereupon he was moved to live in Kuaiji.

s0088.literal: When Wu Mingche was defeated the emperor recalled Jingli's former words and the same day recalled him, again making him Adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Campaign South.
s0088.idiomatic: When Wu Mingche was defeated the emperor recalled Jingli's former words and the same day recalled him, again making him adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Campaign South.

s0089.literal: Within several days he was transferred to Extraordinary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, restored to his original enfeoffment, and entered to hold the post of Minister of Revenue.
s0089.idiomatic: Within several days he was made extraordinary attendant of scattered cavalry and concurrently censor-in-chief, restored to his original enfeoffment, and entered to hold the post of minister of revenue.

s0090.literal: By old form, receiving office was in the afternoon; on the day Jingli took office it happened that the imperial carriage visited the Black Tortoise Observatory; all in office were attending the feast; the emperor feared Jingli would not be at ease and specially ordered early investiture—such was the regard for him.
s0090.idiomatic: By old form, receiving office was in the afternoon; on the day Jingli took office the imperial carriage happened to visit the Black Tortoise Observatory; all in office were at the feast; the emperor feared Jingli would not be at ease and specially ordered early investiture—such was the regard for him.

s0091.literal: That year he died in office, aged sixty.
s0091.idiomatic: That year he died in office, at sixty.

s0092.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies, posthumous title Reverent.
s0092.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of ceremonies with the posthumous name Reverent.

s0093.literal: In the thirteenth year, when he was reburied, he was again posthumously made Central Commander of the Palace Army.
s0093.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when he was reburied, he was again posthumously made central commander of the palace army.

s0094.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he was granted sacrifice in the Founder's temple court.
s0094.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 1 (587) he was granted sacrifice in the Founder's temple court.

s0095.literal: In the second year the imperial carriage personally visited his residence; Jingli was again posthumously made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Center, posthumous title Loyal-Reverent, given one set of pipes and drums, and a stele was erected at the tomb.
s0095.idiomatic: In the second year the imperial carriage personally visited his residence; Jingli was again posthumously made palace attendant and general who pacifies the center, posthumous name Loyal-Reverent, given one set of pipes and drums, and a stele was erected at the tomb.

s0096.literal: In composition Jingli did not favor ornate excess but excelled at narrative; swift to meet the moment, he was praised by his age.
s0096.idiomatic: In composition Jingli did not favor ornate excess but excelled at narrative; swift to meet the moment, he was praised by his age.

s0097.literal: He had a collected writings in thirty juan.
s0097.idiomatic: He left collected writings in thirty juan.

s0099.literal: Liu Shizhi was a native of Xiang in Pei.
s0099.idiomatic: Liu Shizhi came from Xiang in Pei.

s0100.literal: His family for generations was a plain clan.
s0100.idiomatic: His family for generations had been a plain clan.
